verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft is expected to create a powerful sonic boom over Southern California on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Southern Californians may hear a distinct "boom" ... NASA\'s Artemis II'; R5: 'April 10, 2026 ... sonic boom after NASA Artemis II\'s Orion capsule ... California splashdown'; R4: 'sonic booms ... throughout Southern California'
verifications.reasoning: All references directly support Artemis II Orion producing a sonic boom hearable in Southern California on April 10, 2026 (Friday), described as distinct/thunderous.

verifications.claim: The sonic boom occurs during the Artemis II Orion spacecraft's high-speed re-entry at ~24,000 mph.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R3: 'sonic boom, produced as the capsule breaks the sound barrier ... slam into the atmosphere at 30 times the speed of sound' (≈24,000 mph); R2: 'sonic boom as the spacecraft re-enters the atmosphere'
verifications.reasoning: References confirm sonic boom during Artemis II re-entry; 30x speed of sound precisely matches ~24,000 mph.

verifications.claim: The sonic boom occurs around 5 p.m. to 5:15 p.m. PT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'between 5 p.m. and 5:15 p.m.'; R4: 'between 5 and 5:15 p.m. local time'; R5: 'between 5 and 5:15 pm PT Friday'; R1/R3: 'around 5 p.m. Friday'
verifications.reasoning: All references directly state the sonic boom timing as around/between 5-5:15 p.m. PT on the event Friday.

verifications.claim: A video explains how researchers will use the sonic boom from the Artemis II re-entry to calibrate their sensors.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No references mention a video or sensor calibration; they discuss recording with instrumentation and public reports for prediction, but not videos or explicit calibration.
